en:
Alrighty then! So I was down at the lava pits of the Molten Span, testing out my lava suit. Everything was going great. I was even able to swim around in that stuff without suffering a single injury!

So there I am, minding my own business, doing a few backstrokes, when out of nowhere this thing swallows me up whole! Had it not been for my lava suit and built in food pellet dispenser, I would have been done for!

I'm not out of the belly of this beast for more than two minutes and someone is already asking me about my bathroom behavior??? Mister, I'd have smacked you silly for that question had you not been the one to rescue me!

Anyhow! I'm grateful for the assistance. Maybe I can pay you back?
Ain't nothing ever gonna compare to the smell of freshly discharged gunpowder, friend.
Yo, what do you need?
What do yeh' want?
Get away from me, monster!

No! No, no, no! This can't be. I'd rather be dead than Forsaken!

<The Frightened Adventurer raises her weapon, preparing to attack!>
Pleased to meet you! If you like to tinker, you have come to the right place!
Need something?
Water's gift is balance. It cools the burning, softens the hardened, quiets the rattling spirits. When ye can guide that balance in others... ye'll know yer on the true path.

Greetings, adventurer.

I can show you how to weave magic about yourself to change the appearance of your equipment, if you so desire. Do you wish to utilize my services?
Do you require training in the ways of the light?

Ishnu-alah, traveler, and welcome to Nighthaven.

Would you like to browse my selection of fine dresses?

Welcome to Fairweather Stables! I would love to provide you with one of our fine galestriders, but it seems like you may not yet have enough experience to ride one.

They are temperamental at times and are prone to toss newer riders if not handled correctly. I would be more than happy to provide the training for you once you are a more seasoned adventurer and have enough coin!

Welcome to Fairweather Stables! I would love to provide you one of our fine galestriders, but it seems like you may not yet have enough experience to ride one.

They are temperamental at times and are prone to toss newer riders if not handled correctly. I would be more than happy to provide the training for you once you are a more seasoned adventurer and have enough coin!

Yes, I am the renowned trader who magnanimously fed the uh, starving... children...? ...of the Undercity during the recent war with the Scourge. Yes, I am the visionary businessgob and logistical genius who single-handedly armed the resistance and allowed our Dark Lady to found her nation of smelly corpses... um, I mean, "Forsaken."

Yep, I'm him. Glix Xizzix. I'd be happy to sign an autograph. For a small fee, of course.

What am I doing here running a barbershop, you ask? Well I got one word for you, bub--diversification. You've got to keep your revenue streams diversified!
You have shown me your desire, and have payed with precious stone. I will teach you...

You wish to learn the old craft? You wish to smelt dark iron?

Appease me, traveler. Show me a sacrifice and I will consider it!

Your will is strong, and your intent is clear.

Perhaps you are worthy...

Interesting, interesting... I know of a druid that lives atop the hill above the Wailing Caverns, adventurer. She might be able to tell you more about this shard you have found.

Now, I must get back to work!
I am forever denied the touch of stone. I will never again know the glory of shaped iron...
You won't find better equipment anywhere else!
Great ta meet ya.
Need a lift? Our gryphons are always ready to take to the skies.
Lookin' to fish? Then you'll need the proper tools.

Gri'lek, of the Iron Blood

The wanderer. May his strength and lust for battle pierce the ages. 

Gri'lek now dwells far from here. One day, he may return...

Gri'lek, of the Iron Blood

The wanderer. May his strength and lust for battle pierce the ages.

Gri'lek now lingers near the edge of madness...
If Hydraxis recruits more in his war, then it might shift the balance of power...
Have a drink, adventurer. It might be your last!
The Waterlord Hydraxis hides off in Azshara, on an island in the Bay of Storms. What kind of threat can the fool muster from there?
If it weren't for the Grim Guzzler, I'd probably spend my free time pulling the wings off dragon whelps.
If it weren't for the Grim Guzzler, I'd spend my free time pulling the wings off dragon whelps.
The water elementals are at war with the fire elementals, which sort of means they're at war with us. One of their leaders, Hydraxis, is mustering agents for his cause...
I heard that a noble among the water elementals, Hydraxis, wages war with the servants of fire. Let's hope he loses!
Ragnaros will reign supreme!

Hey hey hey! Watch where you're trackin' your shoes.

Tryin' to run a classy establishment here!
Is there something I can help you with?
What is your curiosity looking for?
Have you tried that Thunderbrew Lager? It's good stuff!
It's all guns and flames until someone loses and dies.
I have duty in an hour, but until then... bottom's up!
My father told me there'd be days like this, where a stranger would talk to me and I'd have to restrain myself from killing him.
Be careful, adventurer. There are cultists nearby.
<The gaze of the ranger standing before you is fixed on the enormous anchor pylon in the distance.>
Nostyec Regenthor, mod. E wirsh ador eynes re an tiras an lo vil va novaedi E gol melka ras re y bor rothas aelgestron.

You might think that just because we live on a floating island, there would be no need for miners like me. After so many thousands of years however, we still manage to dig up a lot of interesting things.

It's almost like there's some invisible force, constantly creating new mineral deposits every so often. That's magic for you though, right?

Regardless, if you need training as a miner them I'm your shen'dorei.
I think Plugger filled one of his kegs too much. It looks like it's about to blow!
Don't bother me while I'm partying...
You looking at me, laddy?
I'll take a pint of Dark Iron ale. Oh, you're not the waiter?
Adventurer, how may I further your training in the eyes of the Earth Mother?
Many serve the Earth Mother in different ways. The Earthen Ring and the Cenarion Circle share many similarities and are often aligned in goals, if not methods and customs.
The death of our flesh marked the birth of our spirit and our sacred task.

Hazza'rah, the Dreamweaver.

His is the power of nightmares, and may his foes ever sleep.

Hazza'rah now dreams near the edge of madness.

Hazza'rah, the Dreamweaver.

His is the power of nightmares, and may his foes ever sleep. 

Hazza'rah now dwells far from here. One day, he may return...
How can I help you?
Your talents in cooking are a little too low. Maybe with some practice I can teach you what I know.
Your skills in alchemy aren't yet high enough to benefit from my teachings. Perhaps if you speak with me later...
Well yes, I do know a rare alchemical recipe. Let me teach you!
Hm... yes, I do have a recipe you might find useful. Let me teach you!

Thank you for saving me!

I'm a cook and an alchemist from Stormwind. I was here looking for local herbs and recipes for my uncle Angus when these quilboar captured me. If you hadn't come around, I'm sure I'd have ended up in their stew pot!
Welcome to our humble home. Rest by the fire if ye need to dry off.

No, traveler; only one of his sons is dead. The other lives...


The Outland... Find him there...

I'm afraid that the blade which you hold in your hands is beyond saving. The hatred runs too deep. But do not lose hope, adventurer. Where one chapter has ended, a new one begins.

Find his son - a more devout and pious man you may never meet. It is rumored that he is able to build the Ashbringer anew, without requiring the old, tainted blade.
At last, the curse is lifted. Thank you, hero.

The only way a hero can die, traveler: Through tragedy. The Grand Crusader struck a deal with Kel'Thuzad himself! An ambush would be staged that would result in the death of Mograine. The type of betrayal that could only be a result of the actions of one's most trusted and loved companions.

It was High General Abbendis, High Inquisitor Isillien, and Highlord Mograine that formed the Crusade. In its infancy, the Crusade was a noble order. The madness and insane zealotry that you see now did not exist. It was not until the one known as the Grand Crusader appeared that the wheels of corruption were set in motion.

Because I was there... I was the Highlord's most trusted advisor. I should have known... I felt that something was amiss yet I allowed it to happen. Would you believe that there were a thousand or more Scourge?
You mean, you don't know? The sword that you carry on your back - it is known as Ashbringer; named after its original owner.

The blade and Mograine were a singular entity. Do you understand? This act corrupted the blade and lead to Mograine's own corruption as a death knight of Kel'Thuzad. I swore that if I lived, I would expose the perpetrators of this heinous crime. For two days I remained under the rot and contagion of Scourge - gathering as much strength as possible to escape the razed city.

The Highlord was the lynchpin of the Crusade. Aye, Mograine was called the Ashbringer because of his exploits versus the armies of the Lich King. With only blade and faith, Mograine would walk into whole battalions of undead and emerge unscathed - the ashes of his foes being the only indication that he had been there at all. Do you not understand? The very face of death feared him! It trembled in his presence!

No... He stood in the background, watching as the legion of undead descended upon us. Soon after, my powers were exhausted. I was the first to fall... Surely they would tear me limb from limb as I lay there unconscious; but they ignored me completely, focusing all of their attention on the Highlord.

This was the Ashbringer, fool! As the Scourge began to materialize around us, Mograine's blade began to glow... to hum... the younger Mograine would take that as a sign to make his escape. They descended upon us with a hunger the likes of which I had never seen. Yet...

Aye, I did. Much to the dismay of the lesser Mograine, I made my way back to the Scarlet Monastery. I shouted and screamed. I told the tale to any that would listen. And I would be murdered in cold blood for my actions, dragged to this chamber - the dark secret of the order. But some did listen... some heard my words. Thus was born the Argent Dawn...
The boy had picked up the Ashbringer and driven it through his father's heart as his back was turned. His last words will haunt me forever: "What have you done, Renault? Why would you do this?"
Aye, the lesser Mograine, the one known as the Scarlet Commander, through - what I suspect - the dealings of the Grand Crusader. He led his father to the ambush like a lamb to the slaughter.

It was not enough.


A thousand came and a thousand died. By the Light! By the might of Mograine! He would smite them down as fast as they could come. Through the chaos, I noticed that the lesser Mograine was still there, off in the distance. I called to him, "Help us, Renault! Help your father, boy!"

Aye, the Highlord Mograine: A founder of the original order of the Scarlet Crusade. A knight of unwavering faith and purity; Mograine would be betrayed by his own son and slain by Kel'Thuzad's forces inside Stratholme. It is how I ended up here...

It was all I could do to feign death as the corpses of the Scourge piled upon me. There was darkness and only the muffled sounds of the battle above me. The clashing of iron, the gnashing and grinding... gruesome, terrible sounds. And then there was silence. He called to me! "Fairbanks! Fairbanks where are you? Talk to me Fairbanks!" And then came the sound of incredulousness. The bite of betrayal, traveler...
Surrender to the Light, Adventurer. How can I help you serve today?

Why do they call me "The Breaker"?

Trust me, you don't want to know.

A little bit of a lot of things. Mostly I take the soft and weak and reshape them into hardened fighters once again.

It's a tough world out there, and even our own people mistrust us. We need to be tough and self-reliant if we are to fit into this "horde" with the rest of our people.

Most of the cultists at the Sanctum of Storms seem to have come out to respond to our attack. I never would have expected this to go so well. This was almost too easy...

I think that the Windshapers and High Order have made their push. Valennia should be with them. You should head inside and find her. We'll stay here and keep watch while Valennia and the others finish what they came here to do.
Winds tidings. What can I help you with?
If you seek travel to Auberdine in Darkshore, you have come to the right place. Our people welcome any Alliance members who wish to trade, travel, or aid others in our lands.

In all of our years dealing with the wind spirits, at no point did they speak of the Windlord as a figure of reverence. They acknowledged the existence of a being named Al'Akir, but they avoided invoking his name, almost as if they feared him.

Even if this Al'Akir is an all-powerful "Windlord" or ruler of the wind elementals, my centuries of communion with the spirits has convinced me that at the very least he is not universally loved amongst the denizens of Skywall. I fear that attempting to treat with Al'Akir could merely hasten our doom.

Many disagree on this point. I believe that simple communication is the key. The songs of the wind rang so clearly to us when the spirits where still here. Since they left, its grown quiet and our power as windshapers has weakened.

However, there are those of us who can still hear something. A hushed tone. Fragments of a melody. Those that can still hear and see into the elemental planes must grow in strength. I believe that is the key to our salvation.

Many disagree on this point. I believe that simple communication is the key. The songs of the wind rang so clearly to us when the spirits were still here. Since they left, it's grown quiet and our power as windshapers has weakened.

However, there are those of us who can still hear something. A hushed tone. Fragments of a melody. Those that can still hear and see into the elemental planes must grow in strength. I believe that is the key to our salvation.

Where to begin? Our home is failing. The wards have fallen and the three provinces have begun to drift apart. There was a time not long ago when the spires of Shen'dramar were visible from the western watchtower. No longer. The anchor pylons are weakening, and if the chains finally break...

You must remember that while this realm has been our home for millennia, we will always be somewhat alien to this place. We are not in the terrestrial world that birthed our people. We are in the realm of Skywall, a part of the elemental plane.

We arrived here as the guests of spirits with whom we found common cause in ages past. Now that we Shen'dorei find ourselves bereft of their presence--and potentially--their protection, there's no telling how the other denizens of this plane may perceive us.

Greetings, child. I am Illaya Amberwind and I am the Elder Windshaper here on Zephras Isle. It's always nice to meet young new faces that make their way down from the grove.

Don't let this old shaman hold you up, no doubt you've got many adventures to see to. Do feel free to stop by later if you'd like.

The Cult? They are zealots and killers. They believe that we are being punished for some unspecific sin. The reality is that those that lead them are opportunists leftover from a dubious order of so-called "Priests" of Al'Akir, the Windlord.

They now find themselves in a position to weaponize the fear of our people to consolidate their own power... and they have been quick to do so.

Alas, I have prattled on long enough. Seek out my apprentice Ayessa Dawnsinger in the port of Valanaar if you find yourself out that way. She still hears the song--if only faintly. I am old and much of my power has left me. Ayessa represents the future of our people and the path we must now walk to survive. It's up to her and young skyborne such as yourself to carry the hopes for our people forward.

Greetings, child. I am Illaya Amberwind and I am the Elder Windshaper here on Zephras Isle. It's always nice to meet young new faces that make their way down from the grove.

Don't let this old adventurer hold you up, no doubt you've got many adventures to see to. Do feel free to stop by later if you'd like.

Why is this happening? Put simply, the spirits of the wind just... vanished. They were there one day, and they were gone the next. I can't quite describe the feeling that we windshapers felt when it happened. It was as if a great silence fell over all of us and then... a profound absence.

The petty wraiths you've likely encountered out there are just shades of the glory of the true spirits of wind. Non-sentient, aimless, and a far cry from the kindly spirits we lived in harmony alongside for thousands of years.

You've likely heard that Dalaran is suffering from a magical outbreak, and all of our mages are too preoccupied maintaining the city's wards to effectively contain it.

I'd do anything to protect my city, traveler. Even consorting with the likes of you.
I can teach you to craft fine leather armor, if you have the aptitude.
The spirits have guided you to me. How may I be of service?

Ah, a worldly explorer!

Can you smell that fresh, ocean air? Just don't inhale too deeply. Sometimes it smells a bit fishy.
I don't get too many Skinners in here looking for training, but I guess I could teach you something if you're ready.
Greetings, Adventurer. Do you wish to enter a battle at Darkspear Islands?
I'm working on delicate matters of Horde intelligence. It would be best for us both if you did not disturb me.

No fights goin' on today, pal. The Horde and the Alliance are too busy killin' each other out in the fields when there's perfectly good coin to be made doin' that in my arena! Go figure.

Come back when I get this place up and runnin'.

Welcome, friend, to the barbershop! Come for a cut? A coloring? Something else, perhaps?

We can groom facial hair, perform piercings, ink traveler tattoos, anything you might need!

Have a seat and we'll get right to work. You're only moments away from a new, more attractive you...

<Jim'bek locks eyes with you as he takes a deep puff from his hookah.>

'Ello, mon. Need a rug? A blanket? Or just some cloth for your next project? I got you.
Yo, adventurer, what's good?

I make sure we are provisioned and that the scant resources we do are distributed properly.

If this were a proper order, I'd be something of a quartermaster. Such as we are however, I just do my best to make sure we are at least somewhat equipped to deal with the dangers all around us.

There are many things lurking out there in the dark and the light is needed now more than ever. If only these poor souls could see that just because our world has changed, that doesn't mean we have to be the monsters that the living think we are.

Greetings and well met, Adventurer! Your arrival is timely, and we here at the Durotar Supply and Logistics company are always in need of new contractors.

If you are someone with a knack for gathering useful materials or the skills to craft something from scratch, you have a place here.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

I am glad you asked! We are far more than just a delivery service, Adventurer. We employ and contract craftsman across a variety of specialties and trades, and keep our ear to the ground for any new opportunities to keep their hands busy and goods flowing. We cannot possibly predict the emergent needs of any potential client, so we depend on their crafting orders to arrive to us.

You can imagine that this pipeline is... not as effective as we would hope. We encourage any crafters to satisfy these demands and deliver the goods directly to the customers, wherever they may be. Worry not, you will be fairly compensated for your troubles and earn respect among our organization.

Yes! Well. Sort of.

Gold is the true universal currency, but we have our own system for trade amongst ourselves known as Merchant's Favor. It abstracts away the ever-fluctuating value of gold and silver, and ensures fair and equitable trade between members of the organization. It cannot be liquidated to gold, unless you're engaging in some shady activity, I suppose.

We still use gold for typical day-to-day needs such as materials needed for common crafts, but otherwise rely on Merchant's Favor for any kind of internal commerce.

If you assist us with recovering waylaid crates and ensuring swift fulfillment of craftsman's writs, you will earn plenty!

Recently there has been a sharp rise in lost orders. We strive to ensure that each delivery is efficient and safe, but with a rise of bandits, rowdy creatures, and those damned Alliance, inevitably not every delivery goes according to plan.

Should you find these shipments, take a look over the label for what it should contain. It is not your responsibility to deal with our mistakes, but if you complete the shipment, you will be rewarded in kind.

Dokimi over by the wagon can handle the logistics and your compensation. We will take it from there.

A darkness had fallen over my eyes, but you tore me from my unholy reverie. You saved me, adventurer.

And now I beg you... to forgive me.
Sorry, you don't look like you could fully draw a longbow, nor load a musket. I teach real hunters.

The journal of Jandice Barov is filled with rantings and ravings about the undead. Towards the end of the book is what appears to be a tailoring pattern for the creation of a felcloth bag. This bag is used by warlocks to store soul shards. Do you wish to copy the pattern into your own journal?

The journal of Jandice Barov is filled with rantings and ravings about the undead. Towards the end of the book is what appears to be a tailoring pattern for the creation of a felcloth bag. This bag is used by warlocks to store soul shards. You already know how to create this bag.

The journal of Jandice Barov is filled with rantings and ravings about the undead. Towards the end of the book is what appears to be a tailoring pattern for the creation of a bag of some sort. Your understanding of tailoring is insufficient to decipher the pattern.
Greetings, traveler.

A thousand years ago, when the War of the Shifting Sands ended, three of our kin sacrificed themselves and held the Qiraji inside these halls while Anachronos and Staghelm sealed Ahn'Qiraj shut.

Each of us vowed to look for Merithra, Arygos and Caelestrasz should the Scarab Wall ever fall.

And fall it did... and so we came.

Blast these kobolds. I can't get any work done with them running back and forth, getting in my way. Well, I've got nothing better to do, would you like to learn about mining techniques? Or perhaps you just need some new tools?
There's never an end to the chores around here.

As we were making our way across the Burning Steppes, we were ambushed. It must have been a hundred of them... Dark Iron dwarves! They were shifting out of the walls, from the rocks in the Steppes; out of every crevice, nook, and cranny in sight. They swarmed us, overwhelming the guards and the few brave heroes that had agreed to assist us on this mission.

One thing was clear: This was a highly orchestrated ambush. It was as if they knew every move we would make before we made them...

I suppose... I suppose you are right.

Gor'shak told me that your Warchief has big plans. Plans that may change the way the Alliance and Horde interact. What do you know about this?
She now resides at the side of Emperor Thaurissan. He has her under some sort of powerful thought altering spell... and here I sit, completely helpless.

How else could this have happened? Someone must have tipped the Dark Irons off.


So help me, if I ever get out of here, I will spend the rest of my days finding the traitor.

Where was I? Oh yes, so we were captured. My elite guardsmen were executed on the spot. They spared me and took the princess away by way of ram. I was taken to the detention halls of the Slag Pit and then transferred to this prison.

I can only assume I am still alive because they wish to extract a ransom for my pitiful life. Or maybe out of cruelty, as a way to let me forever play back the events that transpired in my mind. Regret is the cruelest jailor of all, traveler.

Then listen well, traveler.

Several months ago, the Magistrate of Lakeshire sent envoys to Ironforge, pleading with the King for assistance with the Blackrock incursions coming from Redridge and the Burning Steppes.

Princess Moira volunteered to help, against my pleadings. I was assigned twenty elite guardsmen to protect the Princess through the perilous journey from the Loch to Lakeshire.
All is lost...
Do I look stupid to you, traveler? I may as well sign her death warrant myself! Why should I trust you?

We made our way through the Searing Gorge tunnel and into the ravaged wasteland comprising the gorge. In retrospect, things were eerily quiet. The only dangers we ran across were the wildlife of the region: Creatures that my men easily dispatched.

We reached Blackrock Mountain with relative ease and made our way through the stonewrought construction without so much as a hiccup.
My oath binds me to this place. What brings you here, to this light-forsaken place?
Hmm...

Ehh? You look a little too new to be doing business with me.

Come back once you're a bit more familiar with how they do things around here. Trust me.
They named it Bandarion Keep. I wonder what Garek would make of that?
If it bleeds, we can kill it.
Hi there. What can I get for you?

The Thorium Brotherhood possesses the knowledge required to make the sacred arms and armaments of the Fire Lord, but we lack the manpower to obtain the materials required for the crafting.

I, Lokhtos Darkbargainer, have been empowered by the Brotherhood to exchange the exalted recipes for materials gathered from the Molten Core.

Present your offer, traveler.

You see, all you gotta do is forge the Sulfuron hammer and find yourself the Eye of Sulfuras. Combine the Eye of Sulfuras with the Sulfuron hammer and it will become Sulfuras! Now I'm not going to bog you down with any technical information as to where or how or when you can get an Eye of Sulfuras. I'm sure you'll figure that stuff out. Just sign this here contract so that our agreement is binding and our business will be done.

A Sulfuron ingot?!??! Impossible! I must have it! I must! I must!

Traveler, I am authorized to make you a grand deal for that ingot. Perhaps you would be interested to know the secrets of the Hand of Ragnaros? Sulfuras, idiot! The legendary hammer of the Firelord.

In exchange for one Sulfuron Ingot, I am authorized to grant you one copy of the plans to forge a Sulfuron hammer.

Now an adventurer like yourself is probably thinking to himself, "What would I ever need a hammer like that for when what I already own is far superior?"

Well let me tell you something, mister, there ain't nothing more superior than what the Sulfuron hammer can become!
It's simple really. Allow me to summarize...

Do you expect me to cower before the mighty legion of adventurer?

You are nothing to me. Less than nothing. Had I desired your head, it would have been presented to me on a pike.

You have made the mistake that all mortals make.


Time does strange things to those that use it as a form of currency.

In your rush to glory, you assumed that the pace of the game revolved around your actions. Can you even fathom how preposterous that sounds to a being like me? A being that if so inclined could cause your own insignificant thoughts to crush the peanut sized mass of grey matter floating within your skull.
10,000 years of recorded knowledge tends to draw the wrong element to the Athenaeum. Books are stolen, recovered and stolen again on a daily basis.
They've been stolen, traveler! Three of our most prized volumes. Should you return the tomes, a reward will most certainly be yours.

Oh the drama and fuss the young Master exerted. You would think the fate of the world rested squarely on his shoulders. Only mortals could have such a skewed perspective on our world.

Alas, he left me with his meager magical secrets... Librams or some such nonsense. I have no use for these paultry magics but perhaps you might be interested in their enchantments.
What you must understand is that being able to index 10,000 years of existence has given me a rather unique perspective on life. Your present day trials and tribulations are meaningless.

Kildrath tends to overdramatize the situation. For example, "Garona: A Study on Stealth and Treachery," has been stolen over 400 times.

The mark of the Athenaeum protects the tomes, preventing any unauthorized viewings.
Our kind are rare these days, but there are those who still dream in emerald amongst the Shen'dorei.

As I said, the creature that attacked us fled when I singed its backside with lightning, but not before biting Banon. On our way back to town, the Gnolls surrounded us and took us captive.

It wasn't until they started to pull us out of the boat on Fenris Isle that... the change started.

Greetings, adventurer. We've travelled from Moonglade to spread the spirit of the Lunar Festival far and wide.

Won't you join us in our celebration?
Greetings, traveler.

npc: Maestro de embarcadero de la Suma Orden
en: The skycutter that arrives here will take you right to Dalaran City.
Harbor work is open to everyone, but your personal safety is your own responsibility.
We've had trouble with shipments going missing across Azeroth. If you find any, I'd appreciate if you could return them to me.
I sense a disturbance, lurking around you...
Your future is clouded. Concentrate, and ask again.
Your mind is unfocused. Are you hiding something from me?
You don't look like a student...

What'ya need from ol' Mazu'kon, adventurer?
Looking to expand your knowledge? I believe I can help.
I hope that your interruption is for a good cause, I was in the middle of some important work.
Ah, hello. You look as though you have a question for me.
I don't get too many Skinners in here looking for training, but I guess I could teach you something if you're ready.
All will know of what has transpired here in this accursed temple, hero. It will be written about in history books - the tales told as legend from Azeroth to the far reaches of the Nether itself!
Heroes of the Brood? C'Thun must be banished! We can assist you, mortal!
